stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two mangrove species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The red mangrove (Rhizophora mangle) is a tree that grows along tropical coastlines.
• It grows arching prop roots that hold its trunk above the water.
• Its roots help it take in oxygen from the air when the soil is waterlogged.
• The black mangrove (Avicennia germinans) is also a coastal tropical tree.
• It sends up thin, pencil-like roots from the mud.
• Its roots help it take in oxygen from the air when the soil is waterlogged.
• Red mangroves usually grow closest to the sea, while black mangroves grow farther inland.
choices: The red mangrove grows arching prop roots, whereas the black mangrove sends up thin, pencil-like roots from the mud.
The red mangrove and the black mangrove both have roots that help them take in oxygen when the soil is waterlogged.
Red mangroves usually grow closest to the sea, while black mangroves grow farther inland along tropical coastlines.
The black mangrove sends up pencil-like roots from the mud, and these roots help it take in oxygen from the air.
explanation: The goal asks for a similarity, so you need the one feature the two blocks share. Each block says the tree's roots help it take in oxygen when the soil is waterlogged. Choice B names both species and joins them with "both," so it states that shared feature for the pair.

A.why: This is accurate, but "whereas" signals a difference: the two root shapes are not alike. You picked the more vivid detail rather than the feature the trees share.

C.why: This contrasts where the two trees grow, and "while" marks it as a difference. The goal asked for a similarity, so a true contrast doesn't do the job.

D.why: This gives the shared feature for the black mangrove only and never says the red mangrove has it too. A similarity has to cover both items.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two fossil plants. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Archaeopteris is an extinct plant known from fossils.
• It lived about 385 to 359 million years ago.
• It reproduced by releasing spores.
• It grew as a tree with a woody trunk.
• Glossopteris is an extinct plant known from fossils.
• It lived about 299 to 252 million years ago.
• It reproduced using seeds.
• It grew as a tree with a woody trunk.
choices: Archaeopteris reproduced by releasing spores, whereas Glossopteris, a later plant, reproduced using seeds.
Archaeopteris lived about 385 to 359 million years ago, long before Glossopteris first appeared.
Glossopteris, a plant that lived about 299 to 252 million years ago, grew as a tree with a woody trunk.
Archaeopteris and Glossopteris were both plants that grew as trees with woody trunks.
explanation: The two blocks run in parallel, and only one line repeats in both: each plant grew as a tree with a woody trunk. Choice D names both plants and uses "both" to state that shared trait, which is exactly what the goal asks for.

A.why: "Whereas" sets up a difference in how the plants reproduced. It's true, but it's a contrast, and you were asked for a similarity.

B.why: This points out that the plants lived at different times, which is a difference. Mentioning both plants doesn't make a sentence a similarity.

C.why: This gives the shared trait for Glossopteris only. It never says Archaeopteris had a woody trunk too, so no similarity is stated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between woodcuts and etchings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A woodcut is a print made by carving away the surface of a wooden block.
• Ink sits on the raised areas left behind.
• A single woodcut block can be used to print many copies of an image.
• An etching is a print made by using acid to eat lines into a metal plate.
• Ink sits in the sunken lines.
• A single etching plate can be used to print many copies of an image.
choices: Woodcuts and etchings both let an artist print many copies of an image from a single block or plate.
In a woodcut, ink sits on the raised areas, but in an etching, ink sits in the sunken lines.
A woodcut is carved from a wooden block, while an etching is eaten into a metal plate with acid.
An etching plate, whose lines are eaten into the metal with acid, can be used to print many copies.
explanation: Scan the two blocks for the line they share: one block or one plate can print many copies of an image. Choice A covers both techniques with "both" and states that shared feature, so it does what the goal asks.

B.why: "But" marks a contrast in where the ink sits. It's accurate, but it describes a difference, not a similarity.

C.why: This contrasts the materials and methods, and "while" signals the difference. It sounds detailed, but it doesn't do the job the goal names.

D.why: This says only that etchings can print many copies. It leaves out woodcuts, so it never shows that the two share the feature.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two studies' findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2019, economist Lena Park studied warehouse workers in Ohio.
• She examined how a raise in hourly pay affected job turnover, the rate at which workers quit.
• She found that turnover fell after the raise.
• In 2021, economist Tomás Reyes studied restaurant workers in Arizona.
• He examined how predictable weekly schedules affected job turnover.
• He found that turnover fell after schedules became predictable.
choices: Park studied warehouse workers in Ohio, whereas Reyes studied restaurant workers in Arizona two years later.
Park examined a raise in hourly pay, while Reyes examined the effect of predictable weekly schedules.
Park's study and Reyes's study both found that job turnover fell after employers made a change for workers.
Reyes found that turnover among restaurant workers in Arizona fell after their schedules became predictable.
explanation: The goal names the studies' findings. The two blocks studied different workers and different changes, but they end the same way: turnover fell. Choice C names both studies and uses "both" to state that shared finding.

A.why: This contrasts who was studied and when, using "whereas." That's a difference, and it says nothing about what either study found.

B.why: This contrasts what each economist examined. It's a difference in method, not a similarity in findings, and "while" signals that.

D.why: This reports only Reyes's finding. Without Park's matching result, the sentence never shows that the findings are alike.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between P waves and S waves. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• P waves are seismic waves produced by earthquakes.
• They compress and stretch rock as they pass.
• They travel through Earth's interior.
• They can pass through both solids and liquids.
• S waves are seismic waves produced by earthquakes.
• They shake rock from side to side.
• They travel through Earth's interior.
• They can pass only through solids.
• P waves move faster than S waves.
choices: P waves can pass through both solids and liquids, whereas S waves can pass only through solids.
P waves and S waves are both seismic waves from earthquakes that travel through Earth's interior.
P waves move faster than S waves, which shake the rock they pass through from side to side.
S waves, which shake rock from side to side as they pass, travel through Earth's interior.
explanation: Most of the notes describe differences, but each block includes the same line: the waves travel through Earth's interior. Choice B names both kinds of wave and uses "both" to state what they share, which accomplishes the goal.

A.why: "Whereas" sets up a contrast in what the waves can pass through. It's accurate, but it describes a difference, not a similarity.

C.why: This compares the waves' speeds, and "faster than" marks a difference. You picked a true comparison that runs the wrong way for the goal.

D.why: This gives the shared feature for S waves only. It never says P waves also travel through Earth's interior, so no similarity is stated.
